messages:
acme-ops: Hey team — started seeing intermittent 504s and big tail-latency spikes on our Dedicated cluster last night. Example request id: req_8b7f2a3c (2026-02-12T22:14:03Z). Mostly long-context prompts (~8k tokens). We also noticed a pod OOM event on dedicated-infer-4 and GPU memory reported at ~15.6GB/16GB before failure.

support-anya: Thanks — sorry for the trouble. We can pull a repro bundle but need a few quick things to reproduce and triage: exact request id(s), a curl repro, the pod name/node, and short logs (kubectl logs + dmesg/nvidia-smi). Can you paste the curl you used?

acme-ops: Sure. Curl we used (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \\
  -H "x-request-id: req_8b7f2a3c" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"<long prompt>"}' \\
  https://api.redwood-inference.company/v1/generate
```
Response hung ~12s then returned 504. Pod was `dedicated-infer-4` on node `gke-dedicated-01`. Attached a tiny snippet from `kubectl logs`:
```
2026-02-12T22:13:59Z INFO batcher: start batch size=3 seq_len=7800
2026-02-12T22:14:02Z WARN runtime: gpu memory near full (15623 MiB)
2026-02-12T22:14:03Z ERROR runtime: allocation failed -> OOM
```

support-anya: Perfect — that's enough to start. Please run these and paste/upload results:
1) Pod logs + describe: `kubectl -n tenant-42 logs dedicated-infer-4 --previous --tail=500 > pod_logs.txt` and `kubectl -n tenant-42 describe pod dedicated-infer-4 > pod_desc.txt`.
2) Node diagnostics (run on node or ask infra):
```
sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 > dmesg_tail.txt
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.used,memory.free,utilization.gpu --format=csv -lms 1000 -f /tmp/gpu_trace.csv & sleep 10; pkill -f nvidia-smi
```
3) Capture container cgroup memory at the time (if possible): `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/kubepods/.../memory.usage_in_bytes`.
4) Repro curl with `x-request-id` header (the same request id helps correlate).
5) If you can run the redwood helper: `ri-cli collect-support-bundle --request-id req_8b7f2a3c --output logs.tar.gz` and `aws s3 cp logs.tar.gz s3://redwood-support-uploads/acme/req_8b7f2a3c.tar.gz`

sre-liz: Also add `kubectl get pods -o wide -n tenant-42` and `kubectl top node gke-dedicated-01`. If you can, include `dmesg` lines around the time of the OOM — kernel OOM vs cgroup OOM will matter. If it's a GPU OOM (driver-level) we need `dmesg` + `kern.log` + `journalctl -u kubelet --since "2026-02-12T22:10:00"`

eng-ryan: Two quick questions: were you running any large KV-cache enabled sessions or pinned attention cache? Also confirm quantization profile (int8/4) and whether batching settings changed overnight. If you can, add runtime debug env var for one request: `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DEBUG=kvcache,alloc` when restarting the pod to capture allocation traces.

acme-ops: We do use KV cache for some calls. Quantization is int8 by default. No config changes in the last deploy AFAIK. Will try the `ri-cli` and upload. One quick snag — our infra team says they don't have ri-cli on the nodes, so if we run commands from a jump host what's the recommended sequence?

support-anya: If ri-cli isn't available, the manual bundle steps are fine. From jump host: 1) `kubectl cp tenant-42/dedicated-infer-4:/var/log/app /tmp/pod_app_logs` 2) gather `kubectl describe` + `kubectl logs --previous` 3) scp dmesg/journalctl/nvidia-smi CSVs from the node to your jump host and then `tar czf logs.tar.gz pod_app_logs pod_desc.txt dmesg_tail.txt gpu_trace.csv journalctl.txt` 4) `aws s3 cp logs.tar.gz s3://redwood-support-uploads/acme/req_8b7f2a3c.tar.gz --acl bucket-owner-full-control`

ops-bot: Created support ticket #SR-2026-1142 for req_8b7f2a3c and attached initial incident meta.

sre-liz: FYI, if this reproduces consistently you can force smaller batch by setting `MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=4096` in the runtime env to avoid hitting memory cliffs while we investigate.

eng-ryan: If you can reproduce, include the exact reproduced curl + the full `kubectl logs` (not tail) — we need allocation stacks. Also a core dump from the runtime (if safe) would help: `gcore -o /tmp/runtime_core $(pgrep redwood-runtime)` but only if safe to pause the pod — coordinate with support before core dump.

acme-ops: Ok will run checklist now. I can collect logs and upload to s3 within the hour. If we find a consistent repro I'll post the s3 link here. Thanks — will DM infra to run the node commands.

support-anya: Great — once you upload, ping me and I'll request infra node snapshot and a short hotfix (batch cap) rollout to avoid further customer impact. :thumbsup:

acme-ops: Uploaded — s3://redwood-support-uploads/acme/req_8b7f2a3c.tar.gz (will expire in 72h). Posted the reproduce curl and full logs in the bucket.

support-anya: Got it — we retrieved the bundle and started ingestion. Assigning to infra and runtime teams. Tracking in SR-2026-1142. We'll follow up once we have the node snapshot + allocation traces.

eng-ryan: Quick note after skimming bundle: I see repeated `alloc_retry` logs and several `kvcache::evict` events just before the OOM — can you confirm KV cache size for tenant-42? Also which model shard layout (2xA100 vs 4xA10)?

acme-ops: Tenant config: kvcache=enabled, kv_max_size=12GB. Node is 4xA10. Happy to reduce kv_max_size if that helps while you debug.

support-anya: Thanks — we'll start with a soft limit on KV cache + a canary rollout to the node pool. Keeping the ticket open.

acme-ops: Thanks all, appreciate the quick help.
